title: Captivating Foot Sunburst Mehndi Design for Front Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A captivating foot mehndi design tailored for the palm, featuring butterfly wing and petal arrangement. Rated as Easy, this pattern is perfect for a wedding.

The palm has the thickest skin on the hand, so henna stains darkest here. Keep the hand open and relaxed while the paste dries so the lines do not crack or smudge. This is a beginner-friendly pattern: practise the main shapes on paper first, then copy them onto skin with a fine-tipped cone.

Common layouts include an anklet-style band, a trail from the toes to the ankle, and a mandala on the top of the foot. The top of the foot stains lighter than the sole because the skin there is thinner.

Application tips: Dab a lemon and sugar mixture on the dried paste to keep it moist and stuck to the skin. Scrape the dried paste off instead of washing it, and keep the area away from water for the first 12 to 24 hours.

image.alt: Foot Sunburst mehndi design for front hand — captivating henna pattern

faq.q: Is foot mehndi only for brides?
faq.a: No. Simple anklet-style and toe designs are popular for festivals and summer as well.

faq.q: How long does a mehndi stain last?
faq.a: A natural henna stain usually lasts one to three weeks. It fades faster on areas that are washed or rubbed often, such as the hands.

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.

title: Luxurious Foot Ring Pattern Mehndi Design for Front Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A refined foot mehndi design tailored for the palm, featuring mandala and butterfly wing. Rated as Medium, this pattern is perfect for everyday.

The palm has the thickest skin on the hand, so henna stains darkest here. Keep the hand open and relaxed while the paste dries so the lines do not crack or smudge. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.
In South Asian and many Arab weddings, the bride's feet are decorated with henna along with her hands. The soles of the feet, like the palms, have thick skin and take a very dark stain.
